### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/pci/controller/dwc/pcie-tegra194.c`**
   - Removed the inclusion of headers `<linux/pci-acpi.h>` and `<linux/pci-ecam.h>`.
   - Moved the ACPI quirk-related code (including the `tegra194_acpi_init` function and related structures) to a new file, effectively decoupling it from the native driver code.
   - Removed the `#ifdef CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194` preprocessor directive that surrounded the native driver code, allowing it to be compiled regardless of whether it is built as a module or built-in.
   - Moved the definitions of `event_cntr_ctrl_offset` and `event_cntr_data_offset` to be conditionally compiled only if `CONFIG_PCIEASPM` is defined, preventing unused variable warnings when `CONFIG_PCIEASPM` is not set.

2. **File: `drivers/pci/controller/dwc/Makefile`**
   - Restored the Makefile rule for `CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194`, allowing `pcie-tegra194.c` to be built as a module.
   - Changed the rule for building the ACPI-related code from `pcie-tegra194.o` to `pcie-tegra194-acpi.o`, reflecting the separation of the ACPI quirk code into its own file.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes in `pcie-tegra194.c` and the `Makefile` are interrelated. The restoration of the Makefile rule for `CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194` ensures that the native driver can be built as a module, which was broken by the previous commit. 
- The separation of the ACPI quirk code into its own file allows for cleaner organization and compilation, ensuring that the native driver remains independent of ACPI configurations. This separation also addresses the issue of unused variable warnings by conditionally compiling only the necessary parts based on the relevant configuration options.
- Overall, these modifications collectively resolve the build regressions introduced by the previous commit while maintaining the functionality of both the native driver and the ACPI quirks.

Here is the commit message:
PCI: tegra194: Fix MCFG quirk build regressions
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

7f100744749e ("PCI: tegra: Add Tegra194 MCFG quirks for ECAM errata")
caused a few build regressions:

  - 7f100744749e removed the Makefile rule for CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194, so
    pcie-tegra.c can no longer be built as a module.  Restore that rule.

  - 7f100744749e added "#ifdef CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194" around the native
    driver, but that's only set when the driver is built-in (for a module,
    CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194_MODULE is defined).

    The ACPI quirk is completely independent of the rest of the native
    driver, so move the quirk to its own file and remove the #ifdef in the
    native driver.

  - 7f100744749e added symbols that are always defined but used only when
    CONFIG_PCIEASPM, which causes warnings when CONFIG_PCIEASPM is not set:

      drivers/pci/controller/dwc/pcie-tegra194.c:259:18: warning: ‘event_cntr_data_offset’ defined but not used [-Wunused-const-variable=]
      drivers/pci/controller/dwc/pcie-tegra194.c:250:18: warning: ‘event_cntr_ctrl_offset’ defined but not used [-Wunused-const-variable=]
      drivers/pci/controller/dwc/pcie-tegra194.c:243:27: warning: ‘pcie_gen_freq’ defined but not used [-Wunused-const-variable=]

Fixes: 7f100744749e ("PCI: tegra: Add Tegra194 MCFG quirks for ECAM errata")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210610064134.336781-1-jonathanh@nvidia.com
Signed-off-by: Jon Hunter <jonathanh@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Bjorn Helgaas <bhelgaas@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Thierry Reding <treding@nvidia.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the removal of the Makefile rule for `CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194`, which prevented `pcie-tegra194.c` from being built as a module. Additionally, the introduction of `#ifdef CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194` around the native driver code limited its compilation to built-in configurations only, leading to build regressions when attempting to compile as a module. The presence of unused variable warnings was also a contributing factor due to the incorrect conditional compilation of certain symbols.

Here is the patch:
 obj-$(CONFIG_PCIE_HISI_STB) += pcie-histb.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_PCI_MESON) += pci-meson.o
+obj-$(CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194) += pcie-tegra194.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_PCIE_UNIPHIER) += pcie-uniphier.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_PCIE_UNIPHIER_EP) += pcie-uniphier-ep.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_ARM64) += pcie-al.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_ARM64) += pcie-hisi.o
-obj-$(CONFIG_ARM64) += pcie-tegra194.o
+obj-$(CONFIG_ARM64) += pcie-tegra194-acpi.o
 endif
 endif

7f100744749e ("PCI: tegra: Add Tegra194 MCFG quirks for ECAM errata")
caused a few build regressions:

  - 7f100744749e removed the Makefile rule for CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194, so
    pcie-tegra.c can no longer be built as a module.  Restore that rule.

  - 7f100744749e added "#ifdef CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194" around the native
    driver, but that's only set when the driver is built-in (for a module,
    CONFIG_PCIE_TEGRA194_MODULE is defined).

    The ACPI quirk is completely independent of the rest of the native
    driver, so move the quirk to its own file and remove the #ifdef in the
    native driver.

  - 7f100744749e added symbols that are always defined but used only when
    CONFIG_PCIEASPM, which causes warnings when CONFIG_PCIEASPM is not set:

      drivers/pci/controller/dwc/pcie-tegra194.c:259:18: warning: ‘event_cntr_data_offset’ defined but not used [-Wunused-const-variable=]
      drivers/pci/controller/dwc/pcie-tegra194.c:250:18: warning: ‘event_cntr_ctrl_offset’ defined but not used [-Wunused-const-variable=]
